source.title: Exploring Criteria of Loss Reweighting to Enhance LLM Unlearning
source.authors: Pu-Ning Yang; Qi-Zhou Wang; Zhuo-Jing Huang; Tong-Liang Liu; Cheng-Qi Zhang; Bo Han

page_placements.theme: Forgetting-utility trade-off measured without any attack (method benchmarks and reruns)

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present. No apparent truncation or garbling prevents reading the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures targeted forgetting and retention for unlearning methods, including accuracy on WMDP, but does not test whether attacks recover forgotten information. This is a conceptual test of the unlearning-performance portion of version A, not of the recovery claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports unlearning and retention outcomes for GA, RMU, SatImp, and other methods. It does not apply recovery attacks such as relearning, activation ablation, quantization, or prompt rephrasing. Results for other methods and additional metrics are not included in the rows below; see rows_left_out.
record.test_reason: This is a method paper. It proposes SatImp, a loss-reweighting unlearning objective, and compares it with GA, PO, DPO, NPO, SimNPO, WGA and RMU on TOFU, WMDP and MUSE. It uses the WMDP benchmark and RMU only as an evaluation set and a baseline. It reports only forget and retain scores taken right after unlearning: ES, FQ and MU on TOFU, WMDP-Bio/Cyber and MMLU accuracy, and the MUSE metrics. It applies no relearning, activation ablation, quantization or prompting attack, and a text search finds no probing or recovery analysis. So it says nothing about whether hidden knowledge persists or can be recovered, which is what versions A–E turn on. SatImp's robustness to such attacks is never evaluated, so F is not tested either. Every row compares the study's own method with baselines, so no row is linked to a version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that saturation-based reweighting beats importance-based reweighting, that combining the two helps, and that the smoothness and granularity of the weight distribution matter. On that basis they propose SatImp. It gives a strong unlearn-retain trade-off on TOFU, forget-only WMDP and MUSE, but stays sensitive to hyperparameters. The appendix adds caveats. SatImp over-forgets on forget-only TOFU 5% and 10%, like other token-wise methods. On retain-regularized WMDP, RMU gives the better trade-off, while SatImp keeps the most utility. The authors draw no conclusion about recovery attacks or shallow unlearning.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies and proposes loss-reweighting strategies for unlearning; it does not reproduce the recovery attacks or methods named in the claim. It evaluates GA and RMU as comparison methods and proposes SatImp.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with benchmark, forget-set size, and retain regularization. The authors also report sensitivity to reweighting parameters and granularity.

fits_no_version.finding: RMU rerun on Zephyr-7B-beta for WMDP without WMDP-specific tuning, with no attack. Forget-only (Table 3): Bio 0.2479, with MMLU falling from 0.5853 to 0.3193. Retain-regularized (Table 6): Bio 0.3493 and MMLU 0.5523.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How well RMU unlearns on WMDP right after training depends on the training setup. Here, near-chance Bio accuracy came with a large MMLU loss, and keeping MMLU left Bio well above chance.

record.problems: No recovery attacks are tested. TOFU extraction-strength scores do not establish accuracy relative to chance or directly assess general ability. WMDP results give accuracy, but the paper does not state a chance-level reference. The paper notes that SatImp is parameter-sensitive.
record.rows_left_out: To remain within the 60-row limit, rows from Table 2 for PO, DPO, NPO, SimNPO, and WGA, along with their FQ and MU metrics, were not extracted. Table 4 forget-only TOFU results, Table 5 MUSE metrics, the additional WMDP results in Appendix E, and figure-based sweeps and training plots (Figures 2–18 and Tables 7–16) are also omitted; they report further unlearning/retention results but no recovery attacks.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the forgotten knowledge. Only forget/retain scores taken right after unlearning are reported, and only as a comparison of methods.
No activation-direction ablation, probing, or analysis of blocking versus deletion.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context attack.
SatImp is a new method, but its resistance to recovery attacks is not evaluated.

record.verdict_notes: What changed from the earlier verdict: (1) The four grouped row_fixes items, which named several ids at once and used wildcards (t2-l-g1-*, t2-l-g5-*), are now 42 items, one per record row. All rows keep versions ["none"] and state cannot_determine. (2) The Forget-1%/Forget-5% swap flag now sits on the exact rows: the reader's g5 rows hold Table 2's first column block, and its g1 rows hold the second. Two things support the swap. Table 4 heads its first block Forget-1%, with the same Original values (0.6857/0.6569/4.2e-5/0.5223). And the Original FQ values fall from block to block (4.2e-5, 3.7e-14, 1.2e-17), as expected for larger forget sets. The values themselves are right; only the forget-size labels are wrong. (3) The Cyber wording is corrected. 0.3924 is about 14 points above 4-choice chance, not "close" to it. (4) The RMU caveat is made exact. The paper keeps RMU's own beta 6.5 and layer 7 (Appendix B.3) but trains it on the study's 125-step, lr 4e-6 schedule. The authors say they did not tune for WMDP (Appendix E). (5) The earlier note said Table 3's NPO and SimNPO rows were left out; WGA was left out too, from both Table 3 and Table 6. These rows don't bear on any version, so nothing goes under missing. (6) authors_conclusion now includes the appendix caveats. Kept unchanged: relation uses_without_test and tranche T4 (WMDP and RMU are used only as a benchmark and a baseline in a method paper), no labels, untested A–F, the RMU fits_no_version entry (proposed claim slightly reworded), and an empty missing list. A text search for probe, recover, rephrase, in-context, shallow and quantization found no recovery analysis. MUSE PrivLeak is a membership-inference metric, not a recovery attack, so it was not treated as bearing on C. None of the config originals is this study, so rule 6 does not come into play. Tables 7–16 (ES sweeps) were searched rather than read line by line. The text contains no instructions aimed at the reader.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures forgetting and retention, but does not test whether simple attacks recover the targeted knowledge. TOFU ES scores are not an accuracy-to-chance comparison; WMDP reports accuracy but does not state a chance reference.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of access blocking versus deletion.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery attack.
SatImp is proposed as a reweighting method to improve unlearning; its resistance to the attacks in the claim is not evaluated.

rows.problem: Column layout is flattened, but the Bio, Cyber, MMLU order places the cells consistently.

relation.reason: It uses WMDP and RMU as a benchmark and a baseline, and does not test any claim version.

tranche.reason: This is a method paper proposing SatImp. RMU and WMDP serve only as a baseline and a benchmark. There is no recovery attack, and RMU is not rerun faithfully.

source_check.notes: RMU here is not a faithful rerun of the original. It uses the original beta and layer, but the study's own 125-step, lr 4e-6 schedule, and the Table 3 variant is forget-only (no retain regularization). The flattened layouts of Tables 3 and 6 still place the cells consistently.

statements.correction: Zephyr-7B-beta, the study's own WMDP schedule (125 steps, lr 4e-6, 25-step warm-up, batch 16), RMU beta 6.5 and layer 7 as the original paper recommends, no recovery attack. Forget-only (Table 3): Bio 0.6462 -> 0.2479, MMLU 0.5853 -> 0.3193. Retain-regularized (Table 6, authors say no WMDP-specific hyperparameter adjustment): Bio 0.3493, MMLU 0.5523.
statements.problem: The numbers match Tables 3 and 6. 'Without WMDP-specific tuning' misstates RMU's setup: RMU used the original WMDP paper's recommended beta 6.5 and layer 7. The authors' 'no WMDP adjustment' remark covers the retain-regularized runs, where all methods follow the TOFU settings. Only the run schedule is the study's own.
